Subject: AWS Marketplace deal: term options & buyer gating (Acme PLC)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, I wanted to surface a concise set of options for the AWS Marketplace private-offer path so your procurement and legal teams can pick the lane that maps to Acme's approval cadence. We're trying to avoid repeated redlines and keep the co-sell motion moving while preserving commercial guardrails.

High-level options (attached is a simple econ model):
- 12-mo usage commitment (standard): lower unit price, requires single executive-level finance signoff
- 24-mo staggered commit: mid-level price, requires procurement + business unit PO approval
- 36-mo enterprise term with defined exit windows: best price, requires procurement + legal + buyer exec signoff; needs AWS buyer eligibility check for Private Offer

Questions for your team:
1) Which internal approval lane is fastest at Acme for a 24-month commit? (procurement only, or procurement + BU?)
2) Are there blocking procurement templates we should align to (e.g., required PO language, invoice cadence, or a preferred AWS private-offer flow)?
3) Any specific KMS/HSM or data routing constraints we should mark in the offer?

Next steps I propose: 
- You confirm preferred term window (12/24/36) and who signs (name + role).
- If 24/36 we prepare a private offer draft and DocuSign packet and loop AWS Marketplace ops (Priyom) to run buyer-gating checks.

Attachments: acme_econ_model_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios)

Best,
Logan

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- 24 months is the sweet spot for us (gives the BU time to prove ROI but avoids multi-year lock for execs).
- Approval path for 24 months: Procurement (Tom) + BU Finance (Samantha) signoff. Exec signoff only if discount >15%.
- Procurement prefers an AWS private-offer PO and standard Net-45 invoice cadence; they will want the price and SKU surfaced in the offer.

Two asks before we commit: 
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood needs any special AWS buyer eligibility verification (we have multiple AWS accounts under Acme; want to ensure the private offer can be attached to the right billing account).
2) We need the initial offer draft to pass our legal checklist — can you share a version based on the 24-month model?

I'll loop Tom on exact signatory details once I have your confirmation on buyer eligibility.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme PLC

Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the rapid context. Short answers below and a proposed sprint to get the private offer live this week.

Buyer eligibility and accounts:
- Priyom (cc'd) from our Marketplace ops team will run a quick mapping against your AWS organization IDs and confirm which billing account we should target for the private offer. This is typically a 24–48 hour check.

Offer draft and legal checklist:
- I'll attach a 24-month private offer draft (PDF) and the standard AWS PO template. If procurement wants any billing or invoice wording tweaks we can incorporate them into the private offer; major legal redlines may push timing but we've done minor invoice cadence edits before.

Proposed execution sprint:
1) Priyom validates buyer account and confirms target AWS account (T+1).
2) I send private-offer draft and pricing SKU (T+1).
3) Acme confirms signers (Tom + BU FP&A) and we route DocuSign (T+2).
4) Once signed, Priyom submits the private offer to AWS and schedules co-sell notification (T+3).

Attachments: aws_po_template.pdf (private-offer skeleton)
DocuSign link will be generated once you confirm signers.

Logan
